memory_annotations.evidence_summary: For this Denver trip specifically, Maya declines prioritization of an afternoon return because the 2:05 p.m. departure leaves too little margin after a noon client meeting; she chooses the 6:10 p.m. return to allow for an overrun and airport travel.

messages.content: I need to set up flights for a Denver client visit. The rollout review starts Wednesday at 10:30 a.m. and should finish Friday at noon. I can leave Minneapolis after 4:00 Tuesday, and the airfare cap is $690 in economy.
I’ll compare round trips that fit those times and keep the airport transfer in view. Is the review at the client’s downtown Denver office, and will you be checking a bag?
Yes, downtown. Carry-on only. I’d rather not introduce much risk on the way there.

The strongest Tuesday choices are both nonstop: one leaves MSP at 5:25 p.m. and reaches DEN at 7:15 p.m.; the other leaves at 8:15 p.m. and arrives at 10:05 p.m. There is a cheaper itinerary leaving at 4:40 p.m., but it connects with only 42 minutes between flights. Given your Wednesday start, I would drop that connection unless the savings are essential.
Agreed. A missed connection would create too much trouble. What does Friday look like?

The early-afternoon nonstop departs DEN at 2:05 p.m. From downtown, the drive is commonly about 35 to 55 minutes, and Friday traffic can stretch it. Even leaving the meeting at 12:05 would likely put you at the terminal around 12:45 to 1:00, leaving only 65 to 80 minutes before departure. That is possible with a carry-on, but there is little protection if the meeting runs late. The other nonstop leaves at 6:10 p.m. and arrives in Minneapolis at 9:05 p.m.
That gap after the meeting isn’t ideal, but for this trip don’t prioritize an afternoon return. I need enough room for the review to run over, so use the evening flight.

That makes the 6:10 p.m. return the practical choice. You could leave downtown around 3:45 to 4:00 p.m., with additional time available if traffic or security is slow. Paired with that return, the 5:25 p.m. Tuesday outbound is $624 round trip, and the 8:15 p.m. outbound is $578 round trip. Both are nonstop and within the $690 allowance.
Is there any meaningful downside to the cheaper late flight besides getting to the hotel late?

Mostly the arrival hour. After landing at 10:05 p.m., allow roughly 15 to 25 minutes to reach the rideshare pickup area and another 35 to 50 minutes downtown. You would likely reach the hotel around 11:00 to 11:25 p.m. The earlier flight should put you downtown around 8:15 to 8:45 p.m., leaving more recovery time before the 10:30 meeting.
Can you give me the two finalists cleanly, including the usable time around the meeting?

Option 1 is the lower-stress schedule: Tuesday MSP 5:25 p.m. to DEN 7:15 p.m.; Friday DEN 6:10 p.m. to MSP 9:05 p.m.; $624 round trip. You should reach downtown Tuesday before 9:00 p.m., and Friday you have nearly four hours from the scheduled meeting end until departure.

Option 2 is the lower fare: Tuesday MSP 8:15 p.m. to DEN 10:05 p.m.; the same Friday 6:10 p.m. return; $578 round trip. It saves $46 but likely gets you to the hotel after 11:00 p.m. Both avoid connections and stay under policy.
Keep both for now. I’m leaning toward option 1 because the $46 savings doesn’t seem worth the short night. Are these quoted fares inclusive of the standard taxes?
Yes. The $624 and $578 totals include mandatory taxes and fees for economy airfare. Optional seat selection, checked baggage, and any fare-difference protection are not included.
Good. Don’t book yet; I need the project coordinator to confirm the review location today. But those are the two round trips I want to carry forward.

I’ve narrowed the shortlist to the $624 earlier-arrival round trip and the $578 later-arrival round trip, both returning Friday at 6:10 p.m. No reservation has been made. Once the downtown location is confirmed, the transfer assumptions can be checked before ticketing.

No flight has been booked.
